title: Work Stress and Burnout
summary: How draining work feels, how connected the person still feels to it, workload, and the boundaries that protect them.
clinicianNotes: Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

domains.label: Exhaustion
domains.description: Feeling drained by work and not recovering.

guidance.ok: On exhaustion, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On exhaustion, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask about hours, recovery time and what a good week would look like.
guidance.explore: On exhaustion, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask about hours, recovery time and what a good week would look like.

domains.label: Feeling detached
domains.description: Losing interest or feeling numb about work.

guidance.ok: On feeling detached, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On feeling detached, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask what the work used to mean to them and what changed.
guidance.explore: On feeling detached, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask what the work used to mean to them and what changed.

domains.label: Workload and pressure
domains.description: Too much to do, little room for error.

guidance.ok: On workload and pressure, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On workload and pressure, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore which demands could be shared, delayed or dropped.
guidance.explore: On workload and pressure, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore which demands could be shared, delayed or dropped.

domains.label: Boundaries and support
domains.description: Being able to say no, take breaks and talk honestly.

guidance.ok: On boundaries and support, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On boundaries and support, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Explore one boundary the person could try this week.
guidance.explore: On boundaries and support, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Explore one boundary the person could try this week.

items.text: By the end of the working day I feel completely drained.
Even after a day off, I do not feel rested for work.
My job takes more energy than I have to give.
I have stopped caring much about how my work turns out.
I feel cynical or numb about my job.
I dread the start of the working week.
My workload is more than can be done in normal hours.
Work follows me home on my phone or in my head.
I feel I cannot afford to make any mistakes.
I can say no to extra work when I need to.
I take proper breaks during the day.
I have someone at work I can talk to honestly.
